homeIntro: Three quick questions to test what you know about staying safe in a storm.

questions.question: A thunderstorm is starting. Where is the safest place to be?
options: Inside a sturdy building with walls and a roof
questions.explanation: A sturdy building gives real protection. Open fields, lone trees and water make you the easiest path for lightning. (Demo only, not official safety advice.)
questions.sourceLabel: NOAA National Weather Service: Lightning safety

questions.question: After you hear the last thunder, how long should you wait before going back outside?
questions.explanation: Lightning can still strike after the rain stops. A common rule is to wait 30 minutes after the last thunder. (Demo only, not official safety advice.)

questions.question: You can hear thunder. How close is the lightning?
options: Only dangerous if you can also see it
questions.explanation: If you can hear thunder, you are within striking distance. Move indoors right away. (Demo only, not official safety advice.)
questions.sourceLabel: NOAA National Weather Service: Thunderstorm safety
